name: steghide
one_line: hide data inside pictures and audio
plain: `steghide` hides a secret file inside an ordinary JPEG, BMP, WAV or AU file, protected by a passphrase. The picture still looks normal.
In CTFs you meet it as a found picture that may hold a hidden file: steghide info tells you whether something is embedded and steghide extract pulls it out when you know the passphrase.
If you do not know the passphrase, try an empty one, words from the challenge, or guess it with stegseek.
when: Check whether a JPEG or WAV carries hidden data.
Extract a hidden file once you have a passphrase.
Hide a note in a picture to understand the technique.

examples.title: Is anything embedded?
examples.explain: Asks for a passphrase (press Enter for none) and says whether embedded data exists, with its name and size.

examples.title: Extract the hidden file
examples.explain: -sf is the stego file. You are asked for the passphrase; the secret file appears in the current folder.

examples.title: Extract with the passphrase given
examples.explain: -p supplies the passphrase and -xf chooses the name of the extracted file.

examples.title: Hide a file
examples.explain: -cf is the cover file (picture), -ef the file to hide. The picture is changed in place, so keep a copy of the original.

examples.title: Guess passphrases from a list
examples.explain: stegseek is a separate fast tool that tries every word as the passphrase.

options.plain: Show whether data is embedded and details.
List available encryption algorithms and modes.
The cover file (the picture or sound).
The stego file (the output of embed, input of extract).
Do not store the file name.

mistakes: Giving up when the passphrase is unknown: try pressing Enter; many challenges use no passphrase.
Expecting steghide to open PNG: it only works on JPEG, BMP, WAV and AU.
Embedding in your only copy of a picture.
Using steghide for LSB tricks in PNG: that needs zsteg or other tools.
try: Hide a text file in a JPEG, then run steghide info on it.
Run stegseek with a short wordlist on the same file.
see_also: exiftool(1), binwalk(1), strings(1), xxd(1), stegseek(1), zsteg(1), and file(1) to check the real type.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
